small_guidance:
- The current im2col gather loads x with shape [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] which mixes IC/KH/KW along K and N along output positions; this makes x loads non-coalesced across N because adjacent ow positions share the same nb only within a row of OW. Switch the N-tiling so a BLOCK_N tile stays within a single (n, oh) row (e.g. tile OW contiguously and iterate nh outside), making `iw = ow + kw` strides of 1 element and enabling fully coalesced x loads.
- Add smaller/safer autotune entries and bias toward `BLOCK_K=KH*KW*small_IC_chunk` so the inner reduction matches the natural KHW=9 boundary; try configs like `(BLOCK_M=128,BLOCK_N=64,BLOCK_K=36,num_warps=4)` and `(64,128,36)` to align K with KHW multiples and reduce divmod overhead.
- Hoist the `kh,kw,ic` index math out of the K loop by unrolling KH·KW (=9) explicitly and only looping over IC in BLOCK_K-sized chunks; this removes per-iteration `// KHW` / `% KW` arithmetic and lets the compiler keep w/x pointer bases in registers.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an implicit-GEMM conv with layout `NHWC` (channels-last) so the GEMM-K dimension (IC) is contiguous in memory for both x and w; this is the single biggest win for 3x3 fp32 conv on Ampere. Convert input/weight to channels-last once in `__init__` (weight) and at forward entry (input), run the kernel, then return NCHW via a stride-only view. Tile `(OC, N*OH*OW)` with M over OC and N over output pixels; inner loop over IC in BLOCK_K chunks, with KH*KW fully unrolled.
- Fuse conv+bias+ReLU+bias-add fully in the epilogue (already done) but also fold `conv.bias + self.bias.view(-1)` into a single combined bias tensor at forward time (legal: both are added after ReLU? — no, conv bias is pre-ReLU, extra bias is post-ReLU, so keep separate, but precompute `eb` once and pass a single fused bias buffer per call to avoid two loads).
- Consider a persistent-CTA scheme: launch `num_SMs * k` programs and have each loop over `(pid_m, pid_n)` tiles via `tl.program_id(0)` with a swizzled order to improve L2 reuse of weights across output-spatial tiles that share the same OC block.
